verses.text: Around that time, a huge crowd had nothing to eat. Jesus called his disciples over and said,
“I feel for these people. They’ve been with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they’ll collapse on the way. Some of them came a long distance.”
His disciples answered, “Where could anyone get enough bread to feed all these people out here in the wilderness?”
Jesus asked, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
He told the crowd to sit down. He took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and handed them to his disciples to distribute. They passed them out to the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. Jesus blessed them and told the disciples to pass those out too.
Everyone ate and was satisfied. The disciples picked up seven baskets of leftovers.
About four thousand people had eaten. Then Jesus sent them home.
Right away, he got into a boat with his disciples and went to the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came and began arguing with him. They wanted to test him, demanding a sign from heaven.
Jesus sighed deeply and said, “Why does this generation keep demanding a sign? I’m telling you the truth: no sign will be given to this generation.”
Then he left them, got into the boat again, and crossed to the other side.
The disciples had forgotten to bring bread. They had only one loaf with them in the boat.
Jesus warned them, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Herod.”
They discussed this with each other, saying, “He said that because we don’t have bread.”
Jesus knew what they were saying and asked, “Why are you talking about having no bread? Don’t you understand yet? Are your hearts still hard?
You have eyes—can’t you see? You have ears—can’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
When I broke five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of leftovers did you collect?” They said, “Twelve.”
“And when I broke seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets did you collect?” They said, “Seven.”
He asked them, “Do you still not understand?”
They arrived at Bethsaida. Some people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch him.
Jesus took the man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spit on the man’s eyes and laid his hands on him, then asked, “Can you see anything?”
The man looked up and said, “I see people, but they look like trees walking around.”
Jesus laid his hands on the man’s eyes again. He looked intently, his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
Jesus sent him home and said, “Don’t go into the village.”
Jesus and his disciples went to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked them, “Who do people say I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and others say one of the prophets.”
Then Jesus asked them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter replied, “You are the Messiah.”
Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about him.
Then he began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and legal experts, be killed, and rise again after three days.
He spoke plainly about this. Peter took him aside and began correcting him.
But Jesus turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter: “Get behind me, Satan! You’re focused on human concerns, not God’s.”
Jesus called the crowd and his disciples over and said, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must say no to themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me and the good news will save it.
What good is it for someone to gain the whole world but lose their life?
What could anyone give in exchange for their life?
If anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this unfaithful and sinful generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
